== Biography ==
William Glasgow is named as father in five Bengal baptism index entries, four of them with a wife Amelia. William Glasgow born 6 Sep 1825 at Barrackpore, baptised 26 Jan 1826; father William, mother Amelia.<ref name="anc1271490">[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/9899/records/1271490 Ancestry India, Select Births and Baptisms, 1786-1947: William Glasgow, born 6 Sep 1825, Barrackpore, Bengal]. Ancestry index entry; original register uninspected.</ref> Amelia Magdalene Glasgow born 22 Nov 1830, baptised 27 Jul 1831 at Etawah; father William, mother Amelia.<ref name="anc362341">[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/9899/records/362341 Ancestry India, Select Births and Baptisms, 1786-1947: Amelia Magdalene Glasgow, born 22 Nov 1830, Etawah, Bengal]. Ancestry index entry; original register uninspected.</ref> Eliza Graves Glasgow born 5 Aug 1836, baptised 9 Oct 1836 at Serampore; father William, mother Amelia.<ref name="anc247030">[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/9899/records/247030 Ancestry India, Select Births and Baptisms, 1786-1947: Eliza Graves Glasgow, born 5 Aug 1836, Serampore, Bengal]. Ancestry index entry; original register uninspected.</ref> Harrietta Fordyce Glasgow born 11 Oct 1838 at Dehra; father William, mother Amelia.<ref name="anc794514">[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/9899/records/794514 Ancestry India, Select Births and Baptisms, 1786-1947: Harrietta Fordyce Glasgow, born 11 Oct 1838, Dehra, Bengal]. Ancestry index entry; original register uninspected.</ref> George Thomas James Dennis Glasgow born 6 Sep 1840, baptised 8 Oct 1842; father William (no mother named).<ref name="anc1390692">[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/9899/records/1390692 Ancestry India, Select Births and Baptisms, 1786-1947: George Thomas James Dennis Glasgow, born 6 Sep 1840, baptised 8 Oct 1842, Bengal]. Ancestry index entry; original register uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
A2 father review, 2026-11-06: Named only as William Glasgow, father, with a wife Amelia, in Bengal baptisms at Barrackpore (1825), Etawah (1830), Serampore (1836), Dehra (1838) and an unplaced Bengal entry (1840, no mother named). Station-to-station moves of one family are the likely reading, but identity across the entries is a name-and-wife match. Identity hold.

=== Earlier identity hold — superseded 12 November 2026 ===
William is documented as the father in the Bengal William-and-Amelia baptism-index household, 1825–1840. His own father remains Unknown. No military rank, birth, death or General George parentage is selected. The newly located officer records are compatible comparisons, not identified members of this household; Amelia Glasgow-482’s existing 78% father assessment is unchanged.

The FIBIS transcription of the 1835 notice and the 53rd Native Infantry catalogue entry are same-name officer comparisons only; neither is identified with this household.<ref>[https://search.fibis.org/bin/aps_detail.php?id=1439878 FIBIS 1439878, London Gazette, 12 June 1835, p.1127, derivative transcription]; [https://searcharchives.bl.uk/catalog/041-000378735 British Library, IOR/L/MIL/10/35/23], catalogue metadata only. The originals have not been read.</ref>

=== Confident father and officer identity ===
General George Glasgow is the newly selected confident father of William Glasgow in the Bengal William-and-Amelia household, assessed at 95%. Hodson’s printed officer biography explicitly calls William the son of George Glasgow of Greenwich, lieutenant-general Royal Artillery. It records William’s marriage to Amelia Campbell at Barrackpore on 15 October 1824. The held baptism index places William and Amelia’s first known child William at Barrackpore on 6 September 1825, followed by the same parental names at other Bengal stations. This specific wife, station and chronology identifies the officer with the existing documentary father far more securely than name and Bengal alone. The general’s name, rank, corps, Greenwich residence and Quebec service identify the existing General George account. This is a new named father for an already catalogued family, not a first numerical rating of a previously selected father. The 95% is a subjective estimate of the whole father-profile identification, not a measured frequency. The printed 1928 biography was visually inspected; its underlying cadet, marriage and burial originals were not. Hodson states the officer’s parentage directly, while transferring it to the baptism-index household remains an identity inference. It names no mother for William. No Green mother, identity merge or new WikiTree profile is selected. Amelia Glasgow-482’s separate 78% identification and Edward George’s separate 55% father assessment are unchanged. The officer’s 1841 death distinguishes him from the separate 53rd Native Infantry William described as murdered in February 1855; that service file remains unread and is not attached to this father.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3669/page/n278/mode/1up V. C. P. Hodson, List of the Officers of the Bengal Army, 1758–1834, part II (1928), p.273, William Glasgow]. Printed page visually inspected 12 November 2026; underlying historical originals unread.</ref>

William Glasgow (1800–1841), captain, Invalid Establishment, 61st Native Infantry. Born Quebec, Canada, 11 July 1800; cadet 1818; admitted 7 July 1819; ensign 5 February 1819; lieutenant 12 June 1820; captain 5 June 1829; invalided 13 June 1833; died Mussoorie 29 October 1841. Son of George Glasgow of Greenwich, lieutenant-general Royal Artillery. Married Miss Amelia Campbell at Barrackpore on 15 October 1824. Sandhurst cadet. The service paragraph gives transfers through the 31st to the 61st Native Infantry in May 1824. These are Hodson’s statements, not original registers inspected in this review.

=== Original will follow-up ===
The general’s original will, PROB 11/1637/234, inspected 12 November 2026, independently names William among his children. William’s existing father assessment remains 95%. The separate Edward George father assessment has improved from 55% to 78%; the identification of that named son with Emily Caroline’s husband remains probable. [https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/D199415 Will catalogue].
